questions.title: Neuroblastoma is an embryonic tumour
questions.question: Neuroblastoma is a/an:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Neuroblastoma is not an epithelial tumour; it does not arise from surface or glandular epithelium.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Neuroblastoma is not classified with the ordinary mesenchymal tumours (of fat, muscle, bone, cartilage); it belongs to a distinct family defined by embryonic-cell-remnant origin rather than mature mesenchymal tissue.
explanations.C: Correct. Neuroblastoma arises from primitive neural-crest-derived cells of the adrenal medulla and sympathetic ganglia in infants and young children. It is one of the department's five named embryonic tumours -- malignant tumours of primitive, undifferentiated cells derived from embryonic remnants -- alongside retinoblastoma, nephroblastoma, hepatoblastoma and medulloblastoma.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A germ cell tumour (e.g. teratoma, seminoma) arises from totipotent germ cells, a different lineage from the embryonic-remnant cells that give rise to neuroblastoma.

questions.title: Seminoma is not an embryonic tumour
questions.question: The following tumour is NOT an embryonic tumour:

explanations.A: Incorrect (i.e. retinoblastoma IS an embryonic tumour). Retinoblastoma is one of the department's five named embryonic tumours, arising from primitive retinal cell remnants.
explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. medulloblastoma IS an embryonic tumour). Medulloblastoma is one of the department's five named embryonic tumours, arising from primitive neuroectodermal remnants in the cerebellum.
explanations.C: Correct (i.e. seminoma is NOT an embryonic tumour, the exception). Seminoma is a germ cell tumour, arising from totipotent germ cells of the testis, a different tumour family from the department's embryonic-tumour list of neuroblastoma, retinoblastoma, nephroblastoma, hepatoblastoma and medulloblastoma -- malignant tumours of primitive cells derived specifically from embryonic remnants, not germ cells.
explanations.D: Incorrect (i.e. neuroblastoma IS an embryonic tumour). Neuroblastoma is one of the department's five named embryonic tumours, arising from primitive neural-crest remnants.

questions.subtopic: Seminoma excluded from the embryonic tumour family
questions.learning_objective: Recognise seminoma, a germ cell tumour, as not a member of the embryonic tumour family.
